subject: Procurement checkpoint + PO timing for Redwood pilot?
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Procurement checkpoint + PO timing for Redwood pilot?

Hi Sara — thanks again for taking the call this morning. Quick written recap and next steps so we’re all aligned: 

Summary of discovery:
- Goal: pilot Redwood inference for transaction-matching workflows (realtime embeddings + reranking) to reduce manual review.
- Target success metric: 30% reduction in human review time on high-risk queue within first 60 days.
- Expected traffic: ~200k tokens/day initially, scaling to 800k tokens/day if pilot succeeds.

Ask / next steps:
1) Procurement timing: can you confirm whether FinBridge will issue a PO or process via your centralized procurement card? If PO, any internal deadline we should be aware of?
2) Legal / security: Aditya and I can loop in our contracts contact if you’d like a short review of our DPA/Security addendum.
3) Tech sync: propose a 30-minute integration check (engineer-to-engineer) next week to align on KV cache and batching expectations.

Attached: redwood-pricing-sheet-2026-08.pdf (pricing + pilot terms), sow-draft-finbridge-v1.docx (very rough SOW).

If you’re still evaluating internally, no worries — a one-line status update on procurement cadence would help us prioritize capacity for early September.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 415 555 0142

Two quick clarifying Qs: 1) Is procurement the right team to issue a PO or should we expect payment via card/central finance? 2) Any blockers on the SOW draft I sent — happy to tighten scope or remove line items to match your procurement window.

If it helps, I can send a condensed one-page SOW and a PO-friendly invoice template.

Thanks again,
Marissa

Hi Sara — Ben here (Marissa’s manager). I know month-end procurement cycles can be noisy. Two quick items from our side: 

- If FinBridge can confirm a PO or written commitment by Friday Aug 28 we’ll honor the pilot price in redwood-pricing-sheet-2026-08.pdf and reserve capacity for your onboarding window. 
- If timing is tighter, we can optionally convert to a month-to-month pilot on a credit card with an invoice sent to procurement as backup. 

We’ve also got a standard EOU (end-of-window) incentive — we can extend a 10% onboarding credit for agreements executed before the quarter close. Happy to discuss specifics if it helps unblock internal approvals.

Best,

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Final EOQ check-in — priority shifted or still on track?

Sara — quick EOQ check before our internal capacity plan locks next week. We haven’t heard back on procurement timeline or PO cadence; can you share whether the pilot is still a priority for FinBridge this quarter or if approval has shifted to a later window?

If it’s still moving: what’s the single blocker we can help with right now? Examples we’ve seen that speed approvals: a one-page commercial summary for procurement, a pre-signed SOW template for legal, or a short exec note from your side confirming budget availability. We can draft any of the above.

If priorities have shifted, no problem — a one-line note will let us free up reserved capacity and reallocate discounts. If you are returning to this in September, we’ll also keep the SOW draft on hand and can set a new kickoff date.

Thanks for the quick update — we appreciate it either way.

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
